newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to speed reform of state enterprises.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to speed reform of state enterprises.

text.p: The Shanghai city government will accelerate the reform of heavily indebted state enterprises in 1997 with mergers and acquisitions, as well as forcing them into bankrupcy, the Shanghai Securites News said on Thursday.
Listed companies that lost money would be merged and acquired by profit-making enterprises, thus helping the healthier firms raise more working capital, the newspaper said.
The city government also intended to list more local state-owned enterprises on overseas bourses to enhance their ability to raise money and run state assets, it said.
It said another target was to reduce the debts of state enterprises to bring the asset-debt ratio to 60 percent.
In 1996, the average asset-debt ratio for state enterprises throughout China was about 80 percent, according to official figures.
Shanghai's government also wants to establish a social insurance system and a more flexible employment system, the newspaper said without elaborating.
